deep-work-is-valuable.question: Why might a thirty-second email check slow you down even after you reopen a difficult paper?
deep-work-is-valuable.answer: Part of your attention can stay with the message, especially if it raises an unfinished task. You return to the paper before you have fully returned to its argument.

deep-work-is-rare.question: Why might a team reward quick replies even when they interrupt its most valuable work?
deep-work-is-rare.answer: Replies are easy to see. When a team's real output is hard to measure, visible activity can become the evidence people use to judge who is productive.

deep-work-is-meaningful.question: How could a demanding afternoon at work be more absorbing than a free afternoon?
deep-work-is-meaningful.answer: A clear goal, feedback and a challenge that stretches your skills can draw your attention into an activity. An unstructured afternoon may offer fewer conditions for flow.

work-deeply.question: A writer wants to publish two articles. What could she track each week while both are still unfinished, and why?
work-deeply.answer: She could track hours spent writing with full attention. She can change that behavior this week, while a publication count only records a result that arrives later.

embrace-boredom.question: Why keep a scheduled offline interval even when you feel bored and have time to check your messages?
embrace-boredom.answer: Waiting gives you practice resisting the impulse to switch. If boredom always triggers a check, you keep practicing the habit you want to change.

quit-social-media.question: A website occasionally helps you find a good article. What else would you need to know to decide whether to use it regularly?
quit-social-media.answer: Identify the activities that contribute most to your goals. Consider how the site helps or disrupts those activities and whether its benefits outweigh the costs.

drain-the-shallows.question: An unexpected problem takes up an hour you had planned for writing. What should you do with the rest of your schedule, and why?
drain-the-shallows.answer: Redraw the remaining blocks to reflect the time and priorities you now have. The schedule helps you choose how to spend your time and can change as you learn more.
